text: Here is binary search, in Python.
We look up sixteen, thirty-eight and seven. Sixteen and thirty-eight are in the list, yet both come back minus one.
Let's follow sixteen. Two pointers, low and high, mark what is still in play. Each turn, we look at the middle.
Twelve is too small, so low jumps past it. Twenty-three is too big, so high comes down to four.
Now low and high are both four. One candidate left, and it is sixteen. But the loop asks: is low less than high? Four is not less than four. It quits without looking.
The fix is a single character. Less than becomes less than or equal.
Run it again. Sixteen sits at index four. Thirty-eight at six. And seven is still correctly missing.
The rule: while one candidate remains, keep looking. Even when it is the last.
